newsitem.title: USA: CBOT sets Dow 30 futures, options specifications.
newsitem.headline: CBOT sets Dow 30 futures, options specifications.

text.p: The Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) said Thursday its directors approved contract features for the exchange's planned index futures and futures-options on the Dow Jones Industrial Average .DJI.

The contract specifications, approved at a board of directors meeting Wednesday, will be submitted today to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission for approval, in anticipation of the fall launch for the products, the exchange said in a statement.
Dow Jones & Co earlier this month agreed to license its industrial average for investment products at the CBOT, Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE) and American Stock Exchange (AMEX).

The CBOE does not have the specifications set for its options contracts. An AMEX spokesman said Thursday the exchange hopes to have specifications for its unit investment trust ready within the next few weeks.
The CBOT said the futures contract would be valued at $10 times the Dow 30. Based on today's close of 7,777.06 on the Dow, that would be $77,770.60.

The contract will be settled in cash--the settlement price minus the purchase or sale price of the contract--as opposed to physical delivery of stock, and the final settlement price will be set at $10 times a special opening quote of the index.
The DJIA is a price-weighted index of 30 of the largest U.S. stocks.
CBOT DJIA index futures will be quoted in points, with one point equaling $10. Contract months are March, June, September and December.
DJIA futures-options will have quarterly and monthly expirations. The minimum price fluctuation is a half-point, or $5.
The CBOT DJIA contracts will trade from 0830 to 1515 CDT (1330 to 2015 GMT).
In addition, next month the CBOT will launch futures and options based on the U.S. Treasury's new inflation-protected securities.

Treasury will announce the size of its first five-year inflation-protected note sale on July 2, and the CBOT will debut futures and options on inflation-indexed 10-year and five-year Treasury notes July 3 at 0830 CDT/1330 GMT, CBOT officials said.
Treasury's five-year index auction was scheduled for July 8. It already auctioned inflation-indexed 10-year notes in January and April.
The futures contracts will trade within the 10-year and five-year note futures trading pits.
A CBOT official said the CFTC had approved the new contracts, as well as a 30-year product.
The CBOT's 30-year inflation-indexed bond futures and options will not debut until sometime in 1998, when Treasury is expected to begin issuing inflation-indexed bonds, a CBOT official said.
